Thought: I need to understand the definitions of flash point, flame point, and auto-ignition point, and then determine their relative ordering in terms of temperature.

Flash point: The lowest temperature at which a volatile material can vaporize to form an ignitable mixture in air. At this temperature, the vapor may cease to burn when the ignition source is removed.

Flame point (or fire point): The temperature at which the vapor continues to burn after being ignited, even after the ignition source is removed. It is typically a few degrees higher than the flash point.

Auto-ignition point: The temperature at which a substance will ignite spontaneously without any external ignition source. This is typically much higher than both the flash point and flame point.

Based on these definitions, the correct ordering from lowest to highest temperature would be:
Flash point < Flame point < Auto-ignition point
